seo_title: Cost of Living in Prague 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Prague per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The educational and IT capital of Central Europe, with a large post-Soviet diaspora. Since 2022 visas for Russians have been restricted, but a path remains through work or study.
pros: A Schengen country and the centre of Europe — a convenient hub for travel
A large Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking diaspora dating back to Soviet times
A strong education system: international schools and Charles University
Developed healthcare (Motol, Na Homolce) at an EU level
Rent that's affordable relative to other EU capitals
cons: Since 2022 visas for Russians have been heavily restricted
The Russian language is often received coldly after 2022
Czech is mandatory for public services and healthcare

visa_steps.title: D visa or residency
visa_steps.description: For Russians since 2022 — only through work, study or family reunification. Tourists are not admitted.

visa_steps.title: Work: blue card / employee card
visa_steps.description: Residency via a contract with a Czech employer. Processing takes 2–6 months.

visa_steps.title: Study: studentka visa
visa_steps.description: Admission to a Czech university (Charles, CTU, VSE) grants a study visa for the duration of your studies.

visa_steps.title: ICO identifier and Rodne cislo
visa_steps.description: A tax ID and personal number for an account, rental and healthcare.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Ceska sporitelna, CSOB, Komercni banka — they open accounts with residency. Without it — only Revolut and N26.

faq.question: Can I get a visa for Prague in 2026?
faq.answer: A tourist visa — no. Through work, study or family — yes, but with a much longer wait and tighter checks.

faq.question: Where should I live in Prague?
faq.answer: Vinohrady — premium. Zizkov — budget and hipster. Prague 6 — quiet and family-friendly. Karlin — a modern, growing district.

faq.question: Can I move to Prague with kids?
faq.answer: Strong international schools (PBIS, AIS, English College) — from €15,000 a year. Public schools are in Czech.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Prague?
faq.answer: Czech is mandatory for public services and healthcare. English in IT and tourism. Russian is found among the older generation.

faq.question: What are the internet and daily life like in Prague?
faq.answer: Fibre at 250+ Mbps for 600 koruna. Transport is convenient — metro, trams, a monthly pass at 350 koruna.

faq.question: What salary is considered comfortable in Prague?
faq.answer: From 60,000 koruna net for one person, from 100,000 koruna for a family. IT salaries are higher.

reviews.text: I got a blue card before 2022 and moved with my family. It's harder now: companies invite Russians less often. But Prague is convenient — the centre of Europe, with schools and healthcare at a good level.
I got into Charles University and received a study visa. I rent a studio in Zizkov for 18,000 koruna. Classes are in English, and I'm building up my Czech.
